method.method_draft: Use the standard polar-area formula. From the image, note that the displayed curve lies above the x-axis and meets the x-axis at the two boundary points of the region, so the bounded region is swept once as θ runs from 0 to π. From the text, take r = 3θ + sin θ with 0 ≤ θ ≤ π. Since r is nonnegative on this interval, compute the area as A = (1/2)∫_0^π (3θ + sin θ)^2 dθ. Expand the square and integrate term-by-term: 9θ^2, 6θ sin θ, and sin^2 θ, then round the resulting value to three decimals.
